facts.t: Billable weight is the greater of actual weight and dimensional weight. UPS and FedEx figure dimensional weight as length × width × height in inches, divided by 139 for daily rates, and round up to the next pound.
facts.s: UPS Daily Rate and Service Guide

facts.t: USPS applies dimensional weight to Priority Mail, Priority Mail Express and Ground Advantage packages over one cubic foot (1,728 cubic inches), using a divisor of 166.

UPS and FedEx Ground packages can weigh up to 150 lb, be up to 108 inches long, and measure up to 165 inches in length plus girth. Anything beyond that is billed as over maximum limits, with a steep flat fee.
facts.s: UPS Daily Rate and Service Guide

facts.t: Additional Handling usually applies when the longest side is over 48 inches, the second-longest side is over 30 inches, the package weighs over 50 lb, or the packaging is not fully enclosed in corrugated cardboard. Each carrier's service guide has the exact triggers.
The Large Package surcharge kicks in when length plus girth is over 130 inches or length is over 96 inches. Those packages are also billed at a minimum of 90 lb.
facts.s: UPS Daily Rate and Service Guide

facts.t: Girth is twice the width plus twice the height. Length plus girth is the longest side plus that girth.
facts.s: UPS Daily Rate and Service Guide

facts.t: Fuel surcharges change every week. Ground fuel follows the U.S. on-highway diesel price the government publishes, from about two weeks earlier. Air and international fuel follow U.S. Gulf Coast jet fuel. Each carrier publishes a table that turns the fuel price into a percentage.

UPS and FedEx usually announce their general rate increase in September and put it into effect around late December or early January. The headline number is an average: your own increase depends on your weights, zones and surcharges, which often go up more.
USPS changes shipping prices after review by the Postal Regulatory Commission, typically in January and often again mid-year, and runs its own peak-season price increase for the holidays.

Peak season has the same shape every year. Big and heavy packages start paying in late September, every package pays from late October, top rates run from around Thanksgiving week to late December, and fees end by mid-January.

Delivering to a home costs more than delivering to a business. UPS adds a Residential Surcharge, and FedEx Home Delivery has the residential fee built in. Peak season adds a separate residential demand fee on top.

Delivery Area Surcharges apply to ZIP codes on each carrier's DAS list, with higher Extended and Remote tiers. The ZIP lists change, often in the middle of the year, so check the current list rather than last year's.
facts.s: UPS Delivery Area Surcharge ZIP list

facts.t: Domestic parcel zones run from 2 to 8 and are based on the distance from the origin ZIP to the destination. Higher zone means a higher price. Carriers publish zone charts by origin ZIP prefix.
Carriers charge an address correction fee when they have to fix a wrong or incomplete address. Checking addresses before you ship avoids it.
The UPS–Teamsters national contract, ratified in 2023, runs through July 31, 2028. That date is the next big UPS labor deadline.

The United States suspended duty-free de minimis treatment for low-value imports from every country starting August 29, 2025. Small parcels from abroad now owe duties and need customs entries, which changed cross-border e-commerce shipping.

In January 2025, UPS said it would cut the Amazon volume it handles by more than half by the second half of 2026, and reshape its network around more profitable volume. Amazon now runs one of the largest U.S. parcel networks of its own.

FedEx combined FedEx Express, FedEx Ground and FedEx Services into one company, Federal Express Corporation, in June 2024 ("One FedEx"). Network 2.0 is the multi-year program merging their pickup and delivery networks market by market.

In a carrier contract, the discounts on base rates matter less than the fine print: earned-discount tiers based on spend, minimum net charges that cap how low your lightest packages can go, and discounts on surcharges. Each GRI quietly makes all of these weaker unless they're renegotiated.
UPS Ground Saver (which replaced SurePost) and FedEx Ground Economy (formerly SmartPost) are the cheaper, slower home-delivery services for light packages.
